feeds.feed: Initial claims and continued claims, seasonally adjusted and not (the route's insured-unemployment pillar, the count door's claims condition, the closer)
feeds.source: Department of Labor (the UI claims news release; ALFRED vintages after it; the first prints back to August 1975 from the release archive, the bound news releases and volumes, the captures of the Internet Archive, the closing table of the release and the press: collections 45, 399, 396, 382, 397 and 404)
feeds.every: Weekly - Thursday 8:30 AM ET (Wednesday before a Thursday holiday)
feeds.backup: the states' ETA 539 weekly file with the Bureau's seasonal factors (s2/claims_substitute.py, exact where tested; collection 329)
feeds.format_check: q41 feed checks; the claims loader asserts the release week columns (45)

feeds.feed: Unemployment rate, payrolls, the unemployed count, job losers (the household pillar, the payroll pillar, the count door, the job-losers door)
feeds.source: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation (each month as first printed: ALFRED vintages UNRATE, PAYEMS, UNEMPLOY, LNS13023621)
feeds.every: Monthly - usually the first Friday, 8:30 AM ET
feeds.backup: ALFRED's vintage tables appended each release (bhs_update); the last vintage in hand stands until the next; a missing table stops the run (c1021.py); when FRED fails, the BLS API print appended as a vintage (bhs_update, s2/second_source.py; 1043: identical to ALFRED on every month of every table)
feeds.format_check: c1021.py: each vintage read by its dated column; q41 C1021 checks (the thirteen opens, the starter ran today)

feeds.feed: Job openings (the help-wanted pillar: openings growing slower than claims)
feeds.source: Bureau of Labor Statistics, JOLTS (ALFRED JTSJOL, each month as first printed)
feeds.every: Monthly - about five weeks after the month, 10:00 AM ET
feeds.backup: the Indeed Hiring Lab postings index, at most two months (s2/vacancy_bridge.py; collection 330)
feeds.format_check: walk39 asserts the vacancy first prints are not stale (>150 rows, within 8 months)

feeds.source: Federal Reserve, G.17 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (ALFRED INDPRO, each month as first printed)
feeds.backup: the FRED current file of INDPRO (flagged: revised values), then the G.17 release text
feeds.format_check: c1021.py: the newest G.17 print within its ALFRED vintage; the vintage history appended and checked (bhs_update)

feeds.feed: Moody's Baa corporate bond yield, monthly average (the credit pillar)
feeds.source: Federal Reserve H.15 via FRED (BAA); read the 7th of the month after
feeds.every: Monthly - the month's average, posted by FRED on the first business day of the next month; read the 7th
feeds.backup: the FRED monthly series cached (cache/c1021/BAA.csv, private); the cache stands when FRED is unreachable; when FRED fails, two re-publishers on other hosts (macroradar.io, equibles.com), a month taken only where both agree (s2/second_source.py; 1047: equal to FRED on 1294 of 1294 and 82 of 82 months); Moody's itself has no free publisher
feeds.format_check: c1021.py: fredgraph csv parsed by header, a bad parse stops the run; q41 feed checks

feeds.feed: Effective federal funds rate, monthly average (the fed-shock door)
feeds.every: Monthly - the month's average, known the day after month end
feeds.backup: the New York Fed EFFR, monthly calendar-day average (s2/second_source.py; 1043: equal to FRED on 127 of 128 months, never more than 0.01 apart), then the cache
feeds.format_check: c1021.py: fredgraph csv parsed by header; q41 feed checks

feeds.feed: 10-year and 1-year Treasury yields, monthly averages (the job-losers door's witness: the spread negative in any of the prior 12 months)
feeds.source: Federal Reserve H.15 via FRED (GS10, GS1)
feeds.every: Monthly - the month's averages, known the day after month end
feeds.backup: the Treasury daily par yield curve, monthly average (s2/second_source.py; 1043: GS10 equal on 129 of 130 months, GS1 on 130 of 130, never more than 0.01 apart), then the cache
feeds.format_check: c1021.py: fredgraph csv parsed by header; q41 feed checks

feeds.feed: S&P 500 daily close (the market pillar: below its close a year earlier; a confirmation of the claims closer)
feeds.source: Yahoo Finance close at the 5:05 PM ET run, corrected to the official close on FRED (SP500), which FRED posts the same evening, about 8 PM ET
feeds.every: Every trading day - read at the 5:05 PM ET run
feeds.backup: the official FRED SP500 close when the chart feed fails (two independent quotes)
feeds.format_check: q41: reading matches the readings table; two sources compared

feeds.feed: Real GDP (the damage grade's output dimension)
feeds.source: Bureau of Economic Analysis, Gross Domestic Product news release (FRED GDPC1, the latest vintage)
feeds.every: Quarterly - the advance estimate about four weeks after the quarter, revised in each of the next two months; 8:30 AM ET
feeds.backup: GDPNow for the unprinted quarter; the BEA release text
feeds.format_check: damage_dimensions.py: the vintage table read by column name; q41 v3.73 checks

feeds.feed: GDPNow (the output dimension's bridge for the quarter not yet printed)
feeds.source: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, GDPNow (FRED GDPNOW, every update as a vintage)
feeds.every: Several times a month, on the days of the releases it reads (FRED carries each update between about 10:30 AM and 1 PM ET); the Atlanta Fed posts its schedule
feeds.backup: the Atlanta Fed page; the last printed quarter carried
feeds.format_check: the vintage appender names each vintage by its FRED date

feeds.feed: Sahm rule, real time (the comparator on the speed panel)
feeds.every: Monthly - FRED posts it on the morning of the employment report, after the Bureau's 8:30 AM ET release
feeds.backup: computed from the unemployment rate first prints if FRED SAHMREALTIME lapses

channels.channel: initial and continued claims, insured unemployment rate (DOL weekly)
industrial production, the newest G.17 print (the production pillar)
Moody's Baa yield, monthly average (the credit pillar)
the effective federal funds rate, monthly average (the fed-shock door)
the 10-year and 1-year Treasury yields, monthly averages (the job-losers witness)
the unemployed count and job losers, first prints (the count door, the job-losers door)
unemployment rate and payrolls, the newest Employment Situation vintage (the household and payroll pillars)
job openings (BLS JOLTS; the help-wanted pillar)

note: every input the live tool reads, with its backup, schedule, holdings and format guard; the quarterly census reads this and closes the gaps (plan item 15, R1)

tiles.backups: FRED API, then the FRED keyless file, then the file on disk; the BLS API read every run for the six monthly series, compared with FRED, and used for any month FRED lacks
